title: Endoscope objective optical system, US20190261833A1 example 1

design.source_reference: US20190261833A1 EXAMPLE 1, normal observation state (surface table 1 of 10). The publication labels the table EXAMPLE 1, and its various data table carries the d8/d13 pair that this surface table leaves variable

aperture_validity.basis: the source's aperture stop (surface 11) sits at the same plane as surface 10, the flat image-side face of the planoconcave negative lens L4: the publication states 'the aperture stop S is positioned at an apex of an image-side surface of the planoconcave negative lens L4'. A zero-thickness stop row cannot be expressed, so the opening (0.0879 mm, derived from the stated Fno 5.63) is carried as that surface's clear aperture. The import reports no separate aperture-stop member and no stop plate of the design's own is modelled
aperture_validity.consequence: the opening is preserved exactly and the model limits light at that plane by the element's rim, but the record carries no stop plate and is therefore not eligible for stop-dependent evaluation
aperture_validity.satisfaction_basis: no modelled stop plate and no stop-dependent evidence: a stop-dependent match is not available

spectrum.sampling_wavelengths_basis: SOURCE_STATED air wavelength 546.07 nm (the e line: the table heads its index column ne and states vd, and the publication's text says 'ne denotes a refractive index of each lens for a e-line'), converted once to vacuum with the engine's own air model (6432.8 / 2949810 / 25540, material_physics.air_index_exact)
spectrum.wavelength_precision: full precision as used by the Project; rounded values in this document are for display only

sampling_span_nm.note: the source states indices at the e line only. A zero-width interval cannot be filtered, so the span is a +/-0.5 nm window around that one sample; it is a numerical convenience, not a second wavelength and not a measured band

continuous_coverage_nm.note: the source states no operating wavelength range; one e-line index pair per glass does not establish continuous coverage

effective_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial effective focal length of the native Project.

back_focal_length_mm.definition: Signed paraxial distance from the last optical surface vertex to the rear focal point for collimated input.

total_track_mm.definition: Axial distance from the first optical surface to the image plane.

engine_check.method: thick-lens paraxial ABCD through the committed Project's COMPOUND unit

comparison.rule: per quantity: |engine - source| <= atol + rtol * scale, with scale = |EFL| for the effective focal length and max(|BFL|, |EFL|) for the back focal length. atol = 0.005 mm is half a unit in the last decimal of the coarsest focal length these publications print (two decimals); rtol = 2e-3 is 1e-3 for a prescription printed to four decimals on radii as small as 0.27 mm plus 1e-3 for the engine's air-referenced index convention

effective_focal_length_check.note: the source states f to two decimals, so its own rounding is +/-0.005 mm (0.5 %) and the 0.41 % difference is inside that rounding. A matrix trace with the source's absolute indices gives 0.992958 mm, 0.30 % from the stated value; the engine's air-normalised indices account for the rest

back_focal_length.basis: the source states no such first-order value

nominal_effective_focal_length_mm.conditions: the publication's various data table, normal observation state: f = 0.99 (unit mm) at the e line, with the object at 12.00 mm and the spacings d8/d13 of that state

nominal_back_focal_length_mm.definition: from the last surface vertex to the paraxial image point, positive downstream
nominal_back_focal_length_mm.note: the publication states no back focal length

f_number.definition: image-space f-number as the publication states it for the normal observation state
f_number.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's various data table: Fno 5.63)

field.definition: field angle; the full field is twice the largest stated half field
field.basis: SOURCE_STATED (the publication's various data table: omega = 106.8 deg for this state, and the publication's text defines omega as a half angle of view)
field.convention_note: recorded as the source states it. A half field beyond 90 deg means part of the field arrives from behind the object plane, and the stated image height 0.75 mm against f*sin(106.8 deg) = 0.947 mm implies about 21 % barrel distortion, so the pair is consistent only with a very strong fisheye mapping. The record keeps the stated numbers and does not resolve whether omega is a half or a full field

the Project is evaluated at the e line only

the publication states two observation states (normal and magnified) for this prescription and leaves d8 and d13 variable. This record transcribes the normal observation state: d8 = 0.260, d13 = 0.620 and the object distance OBJ = 12.00 mm, from the publication's various data table for that state, which is the column whose f = 0.99, Fno = 5.63 and omega = 106.8 deg this record states. The magnified state (d8 = 0.540, d13 = 0.340, OBJ = 2.85 mm) is not modelled

source surface 10 is a plane with air on both sides and a zero spacing to the stop; it was merged away and its zero spacing added to surface 9's spacing, so no zero-thickness row reaches the format. Surface 9 keeps its glass, so the element's flat rear face is the merged row. Because the merge happened during transcription, the import reports dummy_surfaces 0

the source's stop (surface 11) sits at the apex of the flat image-side face of L4 (source surface 10), so a zero-thickness stop row cannot be expressed and the stop's opening is carried as that surface's clear aperture (0.0879 mm). The opening is preserved exactly; no opaque plate of the stop's own is modelled, which is why design.aperture_validity states STOP_NOT_BLOCKING

the source states no clear aperture. Semi-diameters were derived as an axial beam radius of EFL/(2*F#) = 0.99/(2*5.63) = 0.0879 mm at the stop, growing linearly to the stated image height IH = 0.75 mm at the image plane and back toward the object at the same rate, so the envelope is 0.607 mm at surface 1 and 0.838 mm at the image plane; each clear radius is edged 0.02 mm inside its mechanical radius. They set the stop opening and the solid checks, not the first-order values, and they are not a ray-envelope claim: the field is far outside paraxial validity
nominal prescription surfaces; no figure, centring or surface-roughness error is modelled

warnings: EDGE_THICKNESS_IMPLAUSIBLE (advisory, INFO/WARNING): the derived clear apertures make three elements look thick-edged relative to their clear diameter, L4 (surfaces 7-8, G175844, 0.7408 mm edge), L5 (surfaces 9-STO, G185504, 0.3145 mm edge) and L6 (surfaces 12-13, G197189, 0.7363 mm edge); it is a consequence of the derived semi-diameters on a sub-millimetre objective, not of a stated dimension

notes: project check accepted the committed Project with os-optics 0.14.0

project solids reported no error-severity finding; it reports advisory EDGE_THICKNESS_IMPLAUSIBLE findings on elements whose clear apertures are small relative to their centre thickness, an artefact of the derived (not source-stated) semi-diameters

paraxial is NOT_CHECKED, not MATCHED: the publication states f = 0.99 mm for this state but no back focal length, and the rule requires both quantities. The engine's 0.994034 mm EFL and -0.081796 mm BFL are recorded under first_order.engine_check with the EFL-only comparison and its 37x tolerance ratio

the 0.41 % EFL residual is inside the source's own two-decimal rounding (+/-0.005 mm on 0.99 mm); a matrix trace with the source's absolute indices gives 0.992958 mm, 0.30 % from the stated value, and the engine's air-normalised indices account for the rest
the paraxial focus of the committed Project lies 0.0818 mm before the stated image plane; the source states no BFL, so this is recorded, not resolved
the source's stated half angle of view (106.8 deg) and image height (0.75 mm) are mutually inconsistent under any paraxial mapping (see field.convention_note); the record keeps both as stated

the shared builder writes the Project's evaluation source at its default 587.5618 nm; every value in this record and the paraxial evaluation use the e line (546.219159 nm vacuum). With constant-index materials the two wavelengths give the same indices, so the trace is unaffected
no field verification: this batch built no per-field configurations, so no field-dependent quantity is asserted
